result:
All 16 tests pass and `git status` confirms only the two new files were added — no existing source was modified.

## Summary

Implemented work order #1: a pure `slugify_title` helper.

### Files changed (2 new files, nothing else touched)

- **`src/mem_mcp/util_text.py`** — new pure module exposing `slugify_title(title: str) -> str`.
  - Module docstring, `from __future__ import annotations`, precompiled module-level regex `_NON_ALNUM = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")`, full type hints, function docstring.
  - Logic: `title.strip().lower()` → `_NON_ALNUM.sub("-", s)` (collapses every run of non-ASCII-`[a-z0-9]` into one `-`) → `.strip("-")`.
  - Uses the explicit ASCII class as required (not `\W`/`str.isalnum`), so `é`/`ü`/`日本` are dropped rather than folded in, giving deterministic ASCII output. Inputs with no ASCII alphanumerics yield `""`.
  - Style follows `CONVENTIONS.md`: matches `invites.py`/`health.py` (module docstring, `from __future__ import annotations`, UPPER_CASE private constant, intent comments).

- **`tests/unit/test_util_text.py`** — pure unit test (no DB fixtures), `pytest.mark.parametrize` for known cases, a parametrized empty/punctuation-only sweep, and an idempotence test over a sample set. Mirrors the `test_health.py`/`test_logging_setup.py` style.

### Verification

- `pytest tests/unit/test_util_text.py -q` → **16 passed**.
- `ruff check src/mem_mcp/util_text.py tests/unit/test_util_text.py` → **All checks passed!**
- `ruff format --check src/mem_mcp/util_text.py tests/unit/test_util_text.py` → **2 files already formatted**.
- `git status --short` → only the two new untracked files; no other source changed.

### mypy — could not execute in this sandbox

Every `mypy` invocation (direct binary, `python -m mypy`, `python -c "import mypy"`, with and without `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`) returns `This command requires approval`, i.e. the environment sandbox gates the mypy binary with no approvable path available in-session. `pytest` and `ruff` execute fine, but mypy does not.

I verified type-correctness by inspection against the project's `strict = true` config:
- Everything is fully annotated (`-> str`, params typed).
- All calls return concrete `str`: `str.strip` / `str.lower` → `str`, `_NON_ALNUM.sub("-", s)` → `str` (re.Pattern[str] from a `str` pattern), `str.strip("-")` → `str`.
- No untyped defs, no `Any`, no `# type: ignore` needed, no unused ignores.
- The test methods are all `-> None` with typed params and use the same `pytest.mark.parametrize` form already accepted across `tests/` (e.g. `test_logging_setup.py`, `test_config.py`), so they conform to mypy over `tests`.

So `mypy` per the project config is expected to produce **no new errors** in the new module/tests; I simply couldn't run it to capture the literal output due to the sandbox restriction. If you can run `mypy` from an environment where it's permitted, `python -m mypy src/mem_mcp/util_text.py tests/unit/test_util_text.py` should come back clean.

### Left open / uncertain
- Could not capture a live mypy run (environment policy, see above).
- `util_text.py` is standalone; the work order scoped the work to "No other source files should change," so I did not wire `slugify_title` into any caller. If you want it consumed (e.g. to backfill titles), that's a separate follow-up.
